company_description: About Patna Metro Rail Project Patna Metro Rail, spearheaded by Patna Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (PMRCL), is revolutionizing urban transit in Bihar’s capital through a modern Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS). Phase-1 comprises two strategic corridors: Red Line (East–West Corridor): ~16.86 km, with 14 stations—9.36 km elevated and 7.5 km underground—connecting Danapur Cantonment and Khemnichak. Blue Line (North–South Corridor): ~14.56 km, with 12 stations. The 6.1 km priority stretch (Malahi Pakri to New ISBT) is set to inaugurate in August 2025, with full corridor operations expected by 2027–28. The project is being developed with a robust financial model (20% each from state and center, 60% JICA loan), at an estimated cost of ₹13,400–13,900 crore. Technical specifications include a broad-gauge track system, 25 kV AC overhead electrification, and CBTC signaling, enabling top speeds of 80 km/h and a projected daily ridership of 210,000 commuters. Key players involved: RITES (DPR), DMRC & Egis JV (consultancy), L&T, HCC, YFC–MCL, NCC, Quality Buildcon, KEC, Otis, Johnson Lifts, among others. The priority Blue Line stretch is nearing operational readiness, supported by modern depots, control systems, and passenger-centric station amenities including escalators, lifts, commercial spaces, and enhanced safety measures. ⚠ Disclaimer: This is not an official page of the Patna Metro Rail Project; it is an independent informational and community-driven overview. All information shared is based on publicly available sources and intended to promote awareness about the railway sector.
